title: Best Website Maintenance Services (2026): How to Hire Help
description: How to hire a website maintenance expert: what the service should cover, what to prepare, what drives the price and the red flags.
intro: A website is never really finished. Software needs updates, backups need testing, and small problems appear when you least expect them. Maintenance keeps the site safe, fast and working. It goes wrong when nobody knows what is covered, backups are never tested, or the person with the logins disappears. This guide helps you set it up properly.

faq.q: What does website maintenance usually include?
faq.a: Typically software updates, backups, security checks, uptime monitoring and small fixes. Content changes, new pages and design work may be extra. Ask for a written list of what is and is not included.

faq.q: Do I need maintenance for a site built on a website builder?
faq.a: Less, because the builder handles the software and hosting. You may still want help with content updates, speed, search basics and checking forms and links. WordPress and custom sites need more regular care.

It depends on how often your site changes. A shop or busy blog needs frequent backups; a simple brochure site needs fewer. More important is that backups are stored away from the site and that a restore has actually been tested.

faq.q: What happens if the site gets hacked?
faq.a: Ask whether malware cleanup is included or charged separately, and how quickly the expert responds. A tested backup and a list of all logins make recovery much faster.

faq.q: Should I pay monthly or per task?
faq.a: Monthly plans suit sites that need regular updates and monitoring. Per-task orders suit one-off fixes. Many owners combine a small monthly plan with occasional extra tasks.
